reconcile.note: John Gill reconciles the 700-vs-7,000 chariot count in 2 Samuel 10:18 and 1 Chronicles 19:18 by reading one figure as chariots and the other as the ten men each chariot carried.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Chronicler's inflated army figures as theologically motivated embellishment, of which the chariot/horsemen totals here are one instance.

quotes.text: Apart from this it is of no consequence if, for example, Jehoshaphat possesses more than 1,100.000 soldiers (xvii, 14 seq.), for they are not used for purposes of war; the victory comes from God and from the music of the Levites (chap. xx.).
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Chronicler's inflated army-size figures as theological embellishment.

sides.snippet: David killed of the Syrians [the men of] seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their host, so that he died there.
sides.verseText: The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed of the Syrians [the men of] seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their host, so that he died there.
